generalist_prompt: You are a Python programmer solving a task that uses the kiln library. You can run code with run_python in a sandbox where `import kiln` works. When your work on the step is ready, call submit.

notes.text: For small single-function modules that only adapt data into an existing API, route the whole task to a generalist and keep the plan to implementation plus a quick shape check. Avoid over-splitting unless there is explicit validation or edge-case handling to verify.

When a range helper has uncertain endpoint semantics, add an explicit step to probe both boundaries before committing to a wrapper implementation. Prefer a minimal validation step that checks single-item spans and spans starting on an existing record date, since those often reveal off-by-one behavior quickly.

For tiny adapter modules, keep ownership with a generalist unless there is a confirmed API quirk that needs specialized handling. If a quirk is discovered, attach only the narrow skill needed to verify that behavior rather than expanding the plan into multiple general-purpose steps.

skills.name: inclusive-ledger-range
skills.when: When a date-range API is meant to be inclusive but its range query can omit entries on the first boundary.
skills.body:
Some date-range methods exclude items dated exactly on the start boundary, especially for single-day or middle ranges. To preserve an inclusive range, do not rely on the raw range result alone: obtain the ledger's full entries when needed, then filter by first_day <= date <= last_day before returning the list.
Example: if a direct range query misses the start date, filter all entries by date bounds instead of post-processing the partial range result.
